evidence: Plin. NH 11.180: testūdinī marīnae lingua nūlla nec dentēs

phrases.latin: ēminente tōtō dorsō per tranquilla fluitantēs
phrases.english: floating on the calm sea with the whole shell showing

phrases.latin: pariunt ōva avium ōvīs similia ad centēna numerō eaque dēfossa extrā aquās et cooperta terrā … incubant noctibus
phrases.english: they lay eggs like birds’ eggs, up to a hundred at a time, bury them out of the water, cover them with earth, … and sit on them at night

phrases.latin: Ecce testūdō marīna! Caput ex aquā extollit ut spīret.
phrases.english: Look, a sea turtle! It’s lifting its head out of the water to breathe.

sources: Lewis & Short: testudo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 145, 399.
